proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed exact reuse/collision moments, homogeneous grouped-versus-independent calibration, vanishing-ratio validity, exact half-mean calibration, and finite-null certificates. Four classical source passages were recovered and attested before the resumed D0.5 review; the main math referee passed, but the package remained incremental below the fixed field floor, with witness nondegeneracy still an open rubric finding. The heterogeneous positive-ratio calibration theory needed for field significance is substantial new research; no F stages, Lean proof, or accepted result is claimed.
tldr: Nearest-control matching with replacement separates the threshold for any shared control from the threshold for independent-sign calibration. On the homogeneous Bernoulli population-ATT null family, uniformly over \(p\in[1/4,3/4]\), every positive finite ratio \(m/n\to\lambda\) gives the independent-sign rejection limit \(2\Phi(-z_{0.975}/\sqrt{1+3\lambda/4})>\alpha\), while existing common-control signs give limit \(\alpha\). Both procedures retain the observed studentized statistic and recompute its denominator on every transformation. At constant arm means one half, the grouped randomized rule has exact size \(\alpha\) for every \(m,n\ge2\), and its strict rule is conservative, by invariance derived from the primitive Bernoulli law. Over the entire stated heterogeneous population null \(\mathcal M_0\), the four finite-count size envelopes have attained endpoints and computably certifiable rational approximations. The proved vanishing-ratio theorem gives uniform independent-sign calibration whenever both counts diverge and \(m/n\to0\), including sequences with many collisions. Exact Voronoi moments, a quantitative collision law, and an in-subclass counterexample to supplementary Lemma A.3 support the package. The uniform scalar design and Bernoulli mean band are deliberate benchmark restrictions; broader priority remains provisional.
gap: The common-sign adjustment in \cite{Ferman2021FewTreatedMatching} is specified for shared neighbors, while its inference theorem suppresses sharing. Established reuse-aware variance results do not themselves identify the rejection laws of these two recomputed sign orbits on the same positive-ratio null. The weighted bootstrap of \cite{OtsuRai2017MatchingBootstrap} is an adjacent reuse-preserving comparator that informs positioning; Theorem 1 neither extends nor analyzes that procedure.
fill: Theorem 1 proves that the existing common-sign adjustment repairs positive-ratio distortion in this homogeneous benchmark family, uniformly in the outcome probability. The supporting collision and appendix correction results explain why disappearing sharing is a different requirement. The finite-count heterogeneous benchmark population-null problem remains a first-class open question.
